tools.name: mcp__linear-server__save_comment
tools.description: Create or update a comment on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. If `id` is provided, updates the existing comment; otherwise creates a new one. To start a new thread, pass `body` and exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId` (`statusUpdateType` applies only to `statusUpdateId`; omit it for every other parent) — comments on issues/projects/initiatives become top-level discussion threads; comments on documents/milestones become description comments. A status update holds a single thread, so a comment on an update that already has one is added to it as a reply. To reply to an existing thread, pass `parentId` and `body`; the reply inherits the parent's thread type, so no entity reference is needed. Parent reference fields are ignored when `id` or `parentId` is provided (`statusUpdateType` is rejected instead).

id.description: Comment ID. If provided, updates the existing comment

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Set only together with `statusUpdateId`; omit for issue, project, initiative, document, and milestone comments. Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

parentId.description: Parent comment ID (for replies, only when creating)

body.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe). To embed an image or file, upload it with prepare_file_upload and insert the returned markdown

tools.name: mcp__linear-server__save_issue
tools.description: Create or update a Linear issue. If `id` is provided, updates the existing issue; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `team` is required, and `title` is required unless `template` is set. Note: use `assignee` (not `assigneeId`) to set the assignee — it accepts a user ID, name, email, or "me".

id.description: Only for updating an existing issue. Pass the issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Do NOT pass this parameter when creating a new issue.

title.description: Issue title (required when creating, unless template is set)

description.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe)

patch.description: Partial edits applied to the current content, in order and atomically (one failing operation aborts the whole save). Every anchor string must match the current content exactly once. Only valid on update, in place of the full content/description field

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Must match the current content exactly once

new_string.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the match

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match

anchor.description: Exact text to insert before. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly before the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")

anchor.description: Exact text to insert after. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly after the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")
Text to insert at the very start of the content
Text to insert at the very end of the content

from.description: Exact text where the range starts (inclusive). Must match exactly once

to.description: Exact text where the range ends (exclusive, stays in place). Must match exactly once after `from`

new_string.description: Text replacing the range. Empty string deletes it

team.description: Team name or ID (required when creating)

template.description: Template name or ID. Applied on create only. The template fills in the content, fields, and sub-issues server-side. A `description` replaces the template body rather than merging with it, but an empty `description` keeps the template body. Labels merge with the template's own

cycle.description: Cycle name, number, or ID. Null to remove

project.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug. Null to remove

assignee.description: User ID, name, email, or "me". Null to remove

delegate.description: Agent name or ID. When the user asks to delegate to "Linear" or "the Linear agent", this refers to the "Linear" app user specifically. Null to remove

labels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]). Replaces the full label set; existing labels not included are removed. Omit to leave labels unchanged. Cannot be combined with addLabels/removeLabels; prefer those for incremental changes

addLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to add. Append-only; existing labels are never removed. Cannot be combined with a team change

removeLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue. Cannot be combined with a team change

dueDate.description: Due date (ISO format). On update, pass null to remove the due date

slaBreachesAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the SLA will breach. On update, pass null to remove the SLA

slaType.description: SLA day counting type: "all" or "onlyBusinessDays". Only use with slaBreachesAt; null means unset

parentId.description: Parent issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Null to remove

estimate.description: Issue estimate value. On create, pass null or omit for no estimate. On update, pass null to clear the estimate; omitting leaves it unchanged. 0 is a real estimate only on teams that allow zero estimates.

links.description: Link attachments to add [{url, title}]. Append-only; existing links are never removed

setReleases.description: Replace all releases on the issue with these. Cannot be combined with addReleases/removeReleases

addReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to add. Append-only; existing releases are never removed

removeReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue

blocks.description: Issue IDs/identifiers this blocks. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

blockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers blocking this. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

relatedTo.description: Related issue IDs/identifiers. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

duplicateOf.description: Duplicate of issue ID/identifier. Null to remove

removeBlockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers to remove as blockers of this issue

tools.name: mcp__roam__create_block
tools.description:
Create blocks from markdown content. Target by parentUid, pageTitle, or dailyNotePage (page created if needed). Use nestUnder to insert under a specific child block. Supports nested bulleted lists via markdown indentation.

IMPORTANT: unless you've already called get_graph_guidelines for the target graph this session, call it before using this tool — including for reads. The user's conventions change how to interpret and present results, not just how to write.

Preference: Direct graph mutation. For append-only child blocks where you want Roam-side target visibility first, prefer propose_write_batch (or propose_write for a single branch).

parentUid.description: UID of parent block or page. Exactly one of parentUid, pageTitle, or dailyNotePage is required.

pageTitle.description: Page title to create block under (creates the page if it doesn't exist). Exactly one of parentUid, pageTitle, or dailyNotePage is required.

dailyNotePage.description: Target a daily note page, creating it if needed. Either a date in MM-DD-YYYY format (e.g. '03-17-2026') or a relative day: 'today', 'yesterday', or 'tomorrow' (case-insensitive; resolved to the user's local calendar date). Exactly one of parentUid, pageTitle, or dailyNotePage is required.

nestUnder.description: Insert under a direct child block matching this string (matches on the block's string field, including markup like **bold** or [[links]]). If no match exists, creates a new child block with this text first, then inserts under it. Works with parentUid, pageTitle, or dailyNotePage.

graph.description: Graph to act on, by nickname or name. Optional — if only one graph is available, it is used automatically.

tools.name: mcp__roam__get_block
tools.description:
Get a block's content as markdown. Returns content with <roam> metadata tags containing UIDs - use these for follow-up operations but strip them when showing content to the user. Block refs render as ((uid))<ref>text</ref> where text is the referenced block's content - when writing back, drop the whole <ref>...</ref>, keeping just ((uid)). Show remaining content verbatim, never paraphrase. Use maxDepth for large blocks.

IMPORTANT: unless you've already called get_graph_guidelines for the target graph this session, call it before using this tool — including for reads. The user's conventions change how to interpret and present results, not just how to write.

maxDepth.description: Max depth of children to include in markdown (omit for full tree)

graph.description: Graph to act on, by nickname or name. Optional — if only one graph is available, it is used automatically.

tools.name: mcp__roam__get_node
tools.description: Get complete details for a node by its UID. Returns the title, full block tree (content), creator, creation date, and last modified date.

graph.description: Graph name or nickname.

max_depth.description: Maximum child depth to fetch. Default 10. Increase for deeply nested pages.

tools.name: mcp__roam__get_page
tools.description:
Get a page's content as markdown. Returns content with <roam> metadata tags containing UIDs - use these for follow-up operations but strip them when showing content to the user. Block refs render as ((uid))<ref>text</ref> where text is the referenced block's content - when writing back, drop the whole <ref>...</ref>, keeping just ((uid)). Show remaining content verbatim, never paraphrase. Use maxDepth for large pages.

IMPORTANT: unless you've already called get_graph_guidelines for the target graph this session, call it before using this tool — including for reads. The user's conventions change how to interpret and present results, not just how to write.

title.description: Page title (alternative to uid)

maxDepth.description: Max depth of children to include in markdown (omit for full tree)

graph.description: Graph to act on, by nickname or name. Optional — if only one graph is available, it is used automatically.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__roam__update_block
tools.description:
Update a single existing block's text and display properties (heading, collapse, alignment, children view type). Affects only the block with `uid`: `string` sets that block's literal text — it is NOT expanded into child blocks (unlike create_block/create_page), and the block's existing children are left untouched. To add or restructure children, use create_block / move_block / delete_block.

IMPORTANT: unless you've already called get_graph_guidelines for the target graph this session, call it before using this tool — including for reads. The user's conventions change how to interpret and present results, not just how to write.

string.description: New literal text for this block (the Roam block string, including inline markup like **bold**, [[links]], ((refs))). Set as-is — NOT parsed into nested child blocks. Updates this one block only.

graph.description: Graph to act on, by nickname or name. Optional — if only one graph is available, it is used automatically.

<system-reminder>This memory is 12 days old. Memories are point-in-time observations, not live state — claims about code behavior or file:line citations may be outdated. Verify against current code before asserting as fact.</system-reminder>
1	---
2	name: shared-docs-are-collective
3	description: Never edit a Linear ticket description or similar shared document directly; describe the change and wait for explicit approval.
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: feedback
7	  originSessionId: 2806ae00-9f25-43e4-baca-331d0fc2978c
8	  modified: 2026-10-30T02:22:47.386Z
9	---
10	
11	A Linear ticket's description and its revision history are a collective document the team
12	reads. Do not make major changes to one with a direct edit. Describe the change first,
13	wait for explicit approval, and prefer recording substantial reasoning as a comment over
14	silently rewriting the body.
15	
16	**Why:** teammates read the history to understand how a ticket's scope moved. A unilateral
17	rewrite erases that conversation and presents a conclusion no one agreed to. Said on
18	2026-09-10 after an unapproved rewrite of ENG-2219 that had to be reverted.
19	
20	**How to apply:**
21	- General rule, stated 2026-09-27: never alter an existing ticket's body; add a comment
22	  instead. This covers small additions too. "Add a note in Linear" means a comment, not a
23	  new bullet under Notes (I put a bullet on ENG-2326 and had to move it to a comment).
24	  Creating a new ticket's description is the only exception.
25	- Relaxed 2026-09-29: a fresh ticket still in `Ticket Draft` (not yet approved) may be
26	  edited directly, especially to answer an open question it raised. Use a targeted patch.
27	  Once approved (moved to Triage, Backlog, Todo or later), the comment-only rule applies.
28	  First applied on ENG-2335, replacing its "Unverified dependency" note.
29	- Exception 2026-10-29 (ENG-2440): he had me patch a ticket body he had just approved,
30	  because it was freshly written and nobody else had reviewed it. That is the condition,
31	  not "recent". Once anyone else on the team has reviewed or approved a ticket, scope
32	  shifts must be marked, even sound ones. Only on his explicit instruction.
33	  See [[scope-change-taxonomy]].
34	- "Now let me look at X" is a request to review, not approval. So is silence. Wait for a
35	  clear yes.
36	- When approved, use the smallest targeted patch, not a whole-description replacement, so
37	  the revision diff stays legible. `save_issue`'s `patch` operations do this.
38	- Once implementation settles a ticket's open question, do not even offer to "correct"
39	  the Solution or Notes to match. The decision goes in a comment; the body keeps the
40	  earlier wording so the ticket's evolution stays readable (ENG-2288, 2026-09-22).
41	- The same holds for any shared artifact with a history others read: PR bodies, specs,
42	  design docs. See [[git-operations-are-the-users]], which is the same principle for git
43	  state.
44	
45	- 2026-10-29 (ENG-2442): already past Ticket Draft, but "Nobody else read it, alter the definition directly." What matters is whether anyone else has read the ticket, not its status. If unsure, ask that question instead of defaulting to a comment.

{"id":"ENG-2476","uuid":"3dfc96a8-5a03-4fd5-9410-3df7daaacb7c","title":"Run the schema-versus-migrations check in CI","description":"## Problem

* Nothing in CI checks that `packages/database/supabase/schemas` and `supabase/migrations` describe the same database. `pnpm run check-schema` does this check, but only when a developer remembers to run it locally.
* When the two disagree, the next developer who runs `pnpm run dbdiff:save` gets the unrelated difference in their migration and has to work out where it came from. Reviewers can't see the drift, because a PR diff only shows the changed files.
* <issue id="55189201-4a6b-4be8-98f1-9cca71208f24" label="ENG-2458" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2458/repair-the-sync-between-schema-files-and-migrations" /> had to clean up drift that built up unnoticed (`pg_cron` declared but absent from production, comments lost from migrations). Without a CI check, drift will build up again.

## Solution

* Add a step to `.github/workflows/test-database.yaml` that runs `pnpm run check-schema` in `packages/database`. The workflow already runs on every PR that touches `packages/database/**`.
* `check-schema` runs the sqruff lint, then `pnpm run dbdiff --check`. The diff builds its own shadow database, leaves no file behind, and fails when the schema files differ from the migrations.

## Done When

* `pnpm run check-schema` still passes on `main` when the CI step merges.
* The database workflow runs `check-schema` and fails the PR when the schema files and migrations differ, or when the sqruff lint fails.
* A test PR with a deliberate schema-only change shows the job failing; the job passes again once the change is removed.
* The added CI time is measured and reported in the PR.

## Out of Scope

* Running the check on PRs that don't touch `packages/database/**`.
* Fixing drift found by the check; that goes in its own ticket.
* Installing `sqruff` from one pinned version shared by developers and CI, including from `lintSchemas.ts`. This ticket hard-codes `sqruff==0.44.0` in the workflow, because nothing else in the repository pins it. Decided 2026-11-11; tracked as Roam issue candidate [PXVvu9nW5](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/PXVvu9nW5>).

## Notes

* Prerequisites, all merged: <issue id="36144b5b-b165-42be-9f7c-903b073b5f8d" label="ENG-2461" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2461/move-the-dbdiff-scripts-off-the-deprecated-use-pg-schema-engine" /> (moves `dbdiff` off the deprecated engine, which reported false `GRANT` lines), <issue id="42bee720-daee-405d-b5b4-db817ac61fe2" label="ENG-2459" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2459/remove-the-unused-pg-cron-and-pg-stat-monitor-extensions" /> and <issue id="b6cdab95-9a0c-4ae9-a309-d87f0a9fc09f" label="ENG-2460" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2460/restore-database-comments-missing-from-migrations" /> (remove the known differences), <issue id="81272524-8b3f-4819-a1d2-463250b89650" label="ENG-2467" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2467/lint-all-schema-files-with-sqruff-including-the-large-ones" /> (sqruff lint passes on every schema file). <issue id="8f66abaa-7ae1-4211-a5ab-e93d62cd4452" label="ENG-2457" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2457/fix-dbdiff-failure-caused-by-check-function-bodies-in-conceptsql" /> is another case where a schema change broke `dbdiff` and was found only by hand.
* `check-schema` passes locally on `main` (2b5a11748) plus the migration `20261108120000_alias_my_accounts_inner_table.sql`. That migration was lost when <issue id="81272524-8b3f-4819-a1d2-463250b89650" label="ENG-2467" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2467/lint-all-schema-files-with-sqruff-including-the-large-ones" /> was rebased, so `main` fails the check until it lands. Without it, the diff recreates `my_accounts` and the two functions that depend on it (`author_of_concept`, `author_of_content`).
* Not checked yet: how long the check takes in CI. Locally the diff takes about 8 seconds once the Docker images are present. The workflow already pulls the Supabase images for `pnpm run setup`.
* Source: Roam issue candidate `Gje5TUhGp` in the discourse-graphs graph.

---
name: shared-docs-are-collective
description: Never edit a Linear ticket description or similar shared document directly; describe the change and wait for explicit approval.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 2806ae00-9f25-43e4-baca-331d0fc2978c
  modified: 2026-10-30T02:22:47.386Z
---

A Linear ticket's description and its revision history are a collective document the team
reads. Do not make major changes to one with a direct edit. Describe the change first,
wait for explicit approval, and prefer recording substantial reasoning as a comment over
silently rewriting the body.

**Why:** teammates read the history to understand how a ticket's scope moved. A unilateral
rewrite erases that conversation and presents a conclusion no one agreed to. Said on
2026-09-10 after an unapproved rewrite of ENG-2219 that had to be reverted.

**How to apply:**
- General rule, stated 2026-09-27: never alter an existing ticket's body; add a comment
  instead. This covers small additions too. "Add a note in Linear" means a comment, not a
  new bullet under Notes (I put a bullet on ENG-2326 and had to move it to a comment).
  Creating a new ticket's description is the only exception.
- Relaxed 2026-09-29: a fresh ticket still in `Ticket Draft` (not yet approved) may be
  edited directly, especially to answer an open question it raised. Use a targeted patch.
  Once approved (moved to Triage, Backlog, Todo or later), the comment-only rule applies.
  First applied on ENG-2335, replacing its "Unverified dependency" note.
- Exception 2026-10-29 (ENG-2440): he had me patch a ticket body he had just approved,
  because it was freshly written and nobody else had reviewed it. That is the condition,
  not "recent". Once anyone else on the team has reviewed or approved a ticket, scope
  shifts must be marked, even sound ones. Only on his explicit instruction.
  See [[scope-change-taxonomy]].
- "Now let me look at X" is a request to review, not approval. So is silence. Wait for a
  clear yes.
- When approved, use the smallest targeted patch, not a whole-description replacement, so
  the revision diff stays legible. `save_issue`'s `patch` operations do this.
- Once implementation settles a ticket's open question, do not even offer to "correct"
  the Solution or Notes to match. The decision goes in a comment; the body keeps the
  earlier wording so the ticket's evolution stays readable (ENG-2288, 2026-09-22).
- The same holds for any shared artifact with a history others read: PR bodies, specs,
  design docs. See [[git-operations-are-the-users]], which is the same principle for git
  state.

- 2026-10-29 (ENG-2442): already past Ticket Draft, but "Nobody else read it, alter the definition directly." What matters is whether anyone else has read the ticket, not its status. If unsure, ask that question instead of defaulting to a comment.

message.content: I don't think we need to change the path filter. You said I should do a comment commit in the PR to test the flow, is that not simpler? (And yes to 2)

content.text:
Yes, the test commit is simpler. A commit under `packages/database/**` triggers the workflow, so there's no need to touch the filter.

One catch is in the order of commits. For `pull_request` events, GitHub matches the paths filter against the PR's overall diff, not the latest commit. Once you revert the test commit, the PR no longer touches `packages/database`, so the revert won't trigger a run. You'd get the failing run but never the passing one. This order gets all three runs:

1. **Pass run and timing:** a harmless change under `packages/database` that doesn't change the schema, such as a blank line in `README.md`. The workflow runs and the check passes. That run also gives the CI time.
2. **Drift failure:** a `COMMENT ON` added to a schema file with no migration, written so sqruff accepts it. `dbdiff` fails.
3. **Optional lint failure:** a sqruff violation in a separate commit. It can't go in the same commit as step 2: the lint runs first, and if it fails, `dbdiff` never runs.

Then drop all of them. Step 1's run shows the passing state. A run after the revert wouldn't add anything, and wouldn't trigger anyway.

Now adding the signal-kill case to the candidate. First a read-only Roam call to get its block uids:

content.text:
Two updates, and a correction to the plan for checking it in CI.

**Roam candidate `PXVvu9nW5`:** I added the signal-kill case as an evidence block. It says that when a signal kills `sqruff`, `lintSchemas.ts` exits 0 and the lint passes without running. The proposed approach now also says the script should fail when `sqruff` doesn't finish.

**The test commits:** I'm not changing the path filter, and test commits do trigger the workflow. But a plain revert at the end won't: GitHub matches the paths filter against the whole PR diff, and after the revert that diff no longer touches `packages/database`. So push the commits in this order:

1. **Passing run:** a harmless change under `packages/database`, such as a blank line in `README.md`. The workflow runs and the check passes; this run gives the CI time.
2. **Drift:** add a `COMMENT ON` to a schema file with no migration, and write it so sqruff accepts it. The `dbdiff` check fails.
3. **Optional, lint failure:** a sqruff violation, in a separate commit from step 2. The lint runs first, and when it fails, `dbdiff` never runs.

Then drop all three commits. No run after that is needed, because step 1 already shows the passing state.
